articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions in Modern DC Grids Part 3: Protection and Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper safety and protection in a DC grid is described. It discusses overcurrent and short-circuit protection as well as new methods to make human interaction with the DC safer. The various protection methods must be built into all energy-producing devices that are connected to the DC grid. The protection devices that are required inside the power electronic converters are discussed, as well as galvanic isolation.

articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions in Modern DC Grids Part 2: Control and Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The control in the DC grid is done via power electronics converters. The bidirectional powerflow is dependent on the level of the DC grid voltage and is controlled by the same converters that also have to control the voltage level in the DC grid. The two main power converters, the Interlink and the Grid Manager are described, as well as their internal control methods. The importance of the uncontrolled DC grid in industry is discussed and demonstrated with a practical implementation.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensors and Their Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents some issues about sensors and methods to send wirelessly their measurement data to a user. There are considered the inertial sensors that are available in smartphones but also in other mobile devices. The methods to transmit their measurement data to the user are based on internet or BLE connections. Software resources existing in smartphones or personal computers are presented. Experiments that allow gathering the sensor data using different scenarios of movement are also presented.

articleTitle: Learning Strategies: Experimental Modeling of Laplacian Electric Fields and their Correlation to Kirchhoff's Laws in Physics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Electric field is an abstract notion not fully understood yet by youths, as unnecessary exposure to dangerous situations proves it (train selfies). The paper aims at illustrating mathematical concepts through experiments, designing a resistive grid network. We notice the interconnectivity to Physics, deriving the same equations using Kirchhoff's law and the node potential theorem. A kind of Do-It-Yourself experimental stand has been designed to measure the potential in all nodes of the mesh grid, enabling the design of a mathematical model to describe the phenomena. Experimental stands made at home can be a basis to educational developments, linking ideas that can be shared via the internet, enhancing further the concept of blended learning.

articleTitle: Distance Estimation Using Verilog FPGA Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper approaches a Verilog implementation for distance estimation using an external sensor, HC-SR04 module. The method involves the use of an FPGA with the Nexys4 DDR board. Other implementations, based on microcontrollers or VHDL language are also briefly exposed during the paper as already existing in the domain. This work will emphasize the utility of Verilog implementation of simple systems versus a legacy microcontroller or VHDL approach. Block diagrams, I/O planning, code parts will be presented. At the end some experimental results and conclusions are depicted.

articleTitle: Rotor Flux Estimation for Induction Motors Based on Modified Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for rotor flux estimation with direct applications in the control of induction motors (IM). We propose a new structure for the sliding mode observer (SMO) such that pure integral calculation for flux estimation is avoided. Simulation results, analyzed against performances of conventional SMOs, demonstrate that the proposed observer can directly estimate the rotor flux, and it is robust to parameter variations and load disturbance.

articleTitle: Neural Network-based Wearable Devices for Limb Rehabilitation by Inertial Signal Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Recent progress has led to the widespread use of Machine Learning (ML) in various fields, including biomedical applications. ML can assist in the diagnosis by detecting disease-specific patterns and monitoring the patient's condition. Furthermore, ML algorithms can be implemented on resource-limited systems thanks to emerging technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT), Edge Computing, and wearable devices, enabling real-time disease detection and faster processing. This research explores wearable Neural Network (NN) applications using inertial signals. A multi-purpose wearable device has been developed for arm gesture recognition, fall detection, stair climbing and descending recognition, and gait and physical activity level monitoring. NN-based classifiers have been trained on the Edge Impulse platform and implemented on nRF52840 microcontroller. These classifiers achieved high accuracy (from 95.74% up to 100%), using a small memory portion (from 4.4kB to 9.4 kB of RAM and from 17.4kB to 99.8 kB of Flash memory).

articleTitle: Identifying Developer Positions in AGILE Projects Using BERT Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper is a solution based on machine learning for automatically classifying job titles in AGILE software industry projects. Our methodology incorporates fine-tuning techniques to accurately identify job titles from task descriptions. By utilizing the BERT model, fine-tuned on a dataset of job postings in the software industry, we achieve good performance in understanding contextual information and the semantic nuances of job skills and requirements. The results indicate the model's ability to adapt to various industry projects and accurately identify the project contributors title. These findings highlight the potential of transformer-based models in improving the efficiency and effectiveness of project management practices.

articleTitle: A Buck-Boost Converter with Asymmetric Static Conversion Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel buck-boost converter capable of achieving both higher and lower output voltage compared to the input voltage, depending on the value of the duty cycle. It exhibits an extended step-up capability in the sense that it can boost the output voltage for a wide range of the duty cycle, while the step-down nature is achieved in a narrow interval. The converter is capable to surpass the static conversion ratio of the traditional boost converter if the duty cycle is higher than 0.59, offering greater flexibility and efficiency in applications requiring high voltage gains. The converter was thoroughly analyzed, simulated, and practically implemented to validate its feature, demonstrating its applicability in systems requiring a high static conversion ratio.

articleTitle: Innovative HV Measurement: Noninvasive Digital Tester (NDT) for Enhanced EV Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In electric vehicle (EV) systems, managing multiple high voltage (HV) domains controlled by digital logic ICs presents significant measurement challenges. Traditional HV measurement systems are often complex and costly, requiring the monitoring of numerous simultaneous signals that need to be monitored for each HV domain. This study aims to develop a cost-effective and compact measurement system that simplifies analysis and troubleshooting tasks, focusing exclusively on digital signals. The proposed system consists of an optocoupler, Trigger Schmitt, and shielded cable to ensure accurate signal monitoring. Evaluations were conducted across various frequencies and duty cycles to determine the system's performance in terms of duty cycle error. Results indicate that the system maintains low-duty cycle errors at frequencies up to 500 kHz, making it suitable for high-accuracy applications. At moderate frequencies (1 MHz and 2 MHz), the system performs well at higher duty cycles but shows increased errors at lower duty cycles. At higher frequencies (3 MHz,5 MHz, and 7 MHz), significant errors were observed, particularly at lower duty cycles, indicating a need for further calibration.

articleTitle: Programmable Active Load for Testing DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost solution for the realization of a programmable active load used for testing DC-DC converters with different load profiles. Current control is realized by driving a MOSFET transistor in the active area through an analog control loop. Current value setting and adjustment is realized under the control of an Arduino module that also provides the integration of the active load into a test stand that can execute test sequences described in Python.

articleTitle: Data Acquisition Measurement Experiments using the ADALM2000
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the use of the ADALM2000 module (ADALM2000 Advanced Active Learning Module) in the Data acquisition laboratory by the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> year students of the Faculty of Electronics, Telecommunications and Information Technologies from the Politehnica University of Timisoara. The ADALM2000 module is used to study the operation of a DAC and an ADC. The electrical diagrams of the circuits, the mathematical relationships, the measurements and the calculations that must be performed are presented.

articleTitle: An Ultrareliable Low Computational Method for Detecting the Direction of Emergency Vehicle Sirens Based on an Array of Microphones
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Autonomous driving is becoming more and more advanced and soon it can represent a real solution for reducing traffic accidents and as a result traffic deaths. In the present paper, we present an emergency vehicle direction of arrival detection backup system for the standard detection systems based on computer vision and/or V2X communication technologies. The proposed system is ultrareliable working for a SNR of under -50 dB and it has a low computational complexity compared to the general available methods. Also, the present system can be used to help drivers identify emergency vehicle sound direction of arrival, especially in cars with performant soundproof interiors.

articleTitle: A Method for Comparing Dry Etch Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a verification method to compare the hardware and etch performance of different Oxford Instruments dry etching systems to facilitate etch recipe transfer. The flow-pressure window and the chemical and physical flux within the same flow-pressure window were determined for each system. The chemical and physical fluxes were matched between the investigated systems to yield similar etch results. The method was tested using a continuous SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>/O2 silicon etching recipe.

articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions in Modern DC Grids Part 1: Architecture and Definitions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper gives an overview of possible architectures and definitions for future DC Grids. The differences between the DC Grid and AC Grid are explained in terms of the radial, ring or meshed structure. The advantage of bipolar grids and the reduction of cable weight is discussed. Arguments are given for a recognizable color for the DC cables for both bipolar and unipolar systems. A proposal is done for a voltage level, to meet the requirements in industry, utility, but also to comply with existing IEC normalization regarding maximum voltage levels. Zones where the level of safety is defined by the type of protection, are proposed.

articleTitle: 6G: An Overview of Key Technologies and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The rapid evolution of mobile communication networks continues to revolutionize industries and societies globally, particularly with the advent of fifth generation (5G) technology. Despite these advancements, the escalating demand for data and the emergence of novel applications highlight the need for even more sophisticated and efficient wireless networks. Over the past two decades, each generation of cellular technology has introduced significant changes in operational attributes, including frequency, technology, and speed. As we transition from the voice-centric 1G to the multimedia capabilities of 3G, and the increased mobility and data rates of 4G, the anticipation for 6G technology is growing. The sixth generation (6G) aims to meet unprecedented demands, offering data rates up to 1 Tbps, massive connectivity, ultra-low latency, and enhanced energy efficiency. This article explores the key features, objectives, and anticipated use cases of 6G technology, including holographic communication, extended reality, smart cities, and telemedicine. Furthermore, it delves into the core technologies driving 6G, such as Terahertz communication, blockchain, massive MIMO, quantum communication, and artificial intelligence. Through comprehensive analysis, this study examines the potential challenges and opportunities associated with the deployment of 6G networks, ultimately aiming to provide a roadmap for future research and development in this transformative field.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Deep Learning with Stacked Autoencoders for Cell Line Classification in Microscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper focuses on classifying cell line images using a deep neural network based on stacked autoencoders. The cells are classified into three types: MSC (Mesenchymal Stem Cells), TAF (Tumor-Associated Fibroblasts), and SK-BR-3 (Human Breast Cancer Cells). The implemented methods are: the deep neural network extracts features from the images using its architecture, which consists of two stacked autoencoders with hidden layer sizes of 200 and 100, and a SoftMax layer is used as the final layer to classify the cells. The results achieved with this method are an average accuracy of 96.7% for classifying MSC, TAF, and SK-BR-3 cells. In conclusion, this approach avoids the need for image segmentation, which can be difficult for certain images, that need labeling, and the accuracy of the method depends only on the hidden layer sizes and the number of autoencoders used.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of a Control Method for a ZCS-QRC Buck Topology with Constant Switching Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Quasi resonant converters QRC are useful in a wide range of power management applications, such as DC links, high efficiency DC-DC conversion circuits and so on. For this reason the authors investigated a possible new operation principle for a DC-DC power supply using a classic zero current switching quasi resonant converter ZCS-QRC buck topology. Beside the new detailed possible control technique for a ZCS-QRC, the authors of the paper present an analysis of the operation mode, simulation results to prove the good link between theory and practice, and also conclusions.

articleTitle: A New Step-Up/Down DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new buck-boost topology that contains as semiconductor elements a single MOSFET and three diodes, and as reactive elements two capacitors and three inductors out of which two are coupled. The DC analysis has been performed to derive the static characteristics of the converter. The design equations are provided, and the converter was simulated to prove the feasibility of the proposed architecture, and to validate the theoretical considerations.

articleTitle: A Data-Reuse Regularized Recursive Least-Squares Adaptive Filtering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The recursive least-squares (RLS) algorithm is very popular for adaptive filtering applications, mainly due to its fast convergence rate. The regularized version of this algorithm owns improved robustness features, especially in noisy environments. On the other hand, this robust behavior could influence the tracking capability of the algorithm and its overall convergence performance. To reach a proper balance between these performance criteria, a data-reuse regularized RLS algorithm is proposed in this paper. The specific data-reuse parameter of the resulting algorithm can be used as an additional control mechanism, thus reducing the influence of tuning the main convergence parameter of the RLS filter, which is the forgetting factor. Simulation results obtained in the framework of echo cancellation sustain the performance characteristics.

articleTitle: An Integration Methodology of a Third-Party In-System Programming Solution into a Flying Probe Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This work presents a methodology for integrating a third-party stand-alone In-System Programming (ISP) solution, in this case the Flash Runner Next Generation (FRNXG), with the Takaya APT Flying Probe equipment (FP, model APT1400F). It can serve as a guide for combining other types of external test and measurement devices with the FP machine. The proposed approach extends FP equipment capabilities by offering the advantage of programming supported components, by means of the FP mobile arms. For small, printed circuit boards (PCBs) batches or during the prototyping phase, this solution delivers reduced implementation time and important cost benefits. Our solution exploits the Command Line Execution (CLE) FP communication method, while integrations based on the other available option, namely the Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) calls, are outside of the scope of the present document. Consequently, after physically connecting the FRNXG with the FP machine, programming procedures can be included as a single step within the usual test program. Resulting data is transmitted back to the FP interface and is presented in the default test logfiles. To evaluate the methodology viability, limitations and advantages, experiments were performed on multiple component types, over several weeks. Results were analyzed and discussed in correlation with several experiments performed on PCB batches received from different industry actors. Our conclusions support the suitability of such a solution, if deployed after careful analysis of the industrial context and ISP requirements.

articleTitle: Sensitivity to Measurement Errors of an L-Shaped Phase Array for 3D Localization in Inter-Satellite Links
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The sensitivity analysis of the L-shaped phase array contributes to the deeper understanding of how the measurement errors affects a 3D localization system. First, the proposed 3D localization model in Cartesian coordinate system is given, where for simplicity the origin of the coordinate system is the origin of the L-shaped phase array. The proposed localization method relies on three measurements: range measurement, and line-of sight angles with the x, respectively y axis. The sensitivity analysis revealed that the variation of the L-shaped phase array geometry (variation of the antennas placements) has an impact on the 3D positioning accuracy: a misplaced antenna - placed closer then intended - will have larger line-of-sight error for small distances/ranges in the presence of range measurement errors. Notably, a misplaced antenna will result larger line-of-sight error for large distances/ranges when phase measurement errors occur.

articleTitle: CIC Filter Implementations for FPGA-Based PDM Microphone Systems Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper examines the implementation and resource utilization of Cascaded Integrator-Comb (CIC) filters within FPGA-based Pulse Density Modulation (PDM) microphone applications. Two CIC filter designs were analyzed: one generated using MATLAB's HDL Coder toolbox and the other via AMD's CIC Compiler IP. The study compares the efficiency of both implementations in terms of slice LUTs and slice registers usage. The results demonstrate that MATLAB-generated filters require fewer FPGA resources, offering more flexibility, while CIC Compiler filters provide optimized multi-channel support and the option to utilize DSP48 slices for enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Vegetation Indices as Discriminators Between Different Crop Categories
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Monitoring vegetation health is crucial for assessing ecosystem stability amidst climate change and environmental degradation. Hyperspectral imaging provides detailed data that can be systematized using various vegetation indices. Vegetation indices represent expert-determined values with relevance in analyzing plant growth and vigor dynamics or in sensing plant water status, among others. Many practical applications are built upon analysis of vegetation indices values. In this paper we investigate their discriminative power as features of a classifier and what is their relative importance in this discrimination. The proposed method involves a random forest classifier and is evaluated in context of agriculture crop segmentation on UAV-HSI database. Results indicate medium-to-strong discriminative power and relatively comparable importance, with none of the indices being dominant.

articleTitle: A Learning Experience Platform for a Technical University
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we present a Learning Experience Platform (LXP) model suggested to a technical university, leveraging the existing LMS as a foundation. The LXP model aims to enhance student engagement, personalize learning experiences, and foster a more collaborative and interactive learning environment. The paper outlines the key components of the proposed LXP model. To validate the proposed model, a pilot study was conducted involving a group of students from a technical university. The students' perceptions of the LMS and LXP were evaluated through a survey. The findings of the study provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of the LXP model in meeting the needs of technical university students and inform future development and implementation efforts.

articleTitle: Increasing of Specific Energy of the Supercapacitors Based on Cellulose-Derived Nanostructures and Conductive Polymers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Mechanism analysis of the electrostatic double-layer capacitance and electrochemical pseudocapacitance of specific supercapacitors has been performed in this paper. The amount of stored energy is influenced by a set of structural parameters, which characterize the electrode/electrolyte nature, and these parameters have been correlated. Materials based on cellulose-derived nanostructures and conductive polymers were studied. The chemistry of the polymer chains and functional groups has been considered for structural simulation with the HFSS program. The obtained parametrical dependences of the specific energy helped us to decide better material configuration for energetic performance. The ionic conductivity was estimated for different sets of materials. The values for specific energy were obtained up to 24 W h/kg in comparison with the reported values with non-correlated parameters of maximum 21.7 W h/kg, for excitations of about 10 A/g current density. Parameters' correlation impact is significant and can be revealed by the non-invasive simulation method.

articleTitle: XTEA Brute-Force Cracker for FPGA in HLS and HDL
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This work presents a study comparing Extended Tiny Encryption Algorithm (XTEA) brute-force cracker C++/hlsand Verilog/HDL implementations on FPGA. The HDL-based implementation outperformed the HLS-based implementation by a factor of 2.8, and it also demonstrated exceptionally low total power dissipation compared to both CPU and GPU implementations.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Optimal Features for CLAHE Algorithm on Post-COVID19 CT Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a statistical analysis of the parameters most suited to display an accurate Computed Tomograph (CT) scans. Several scans on patients affected by the Sars-CoV2 virus have been investigated with the final aim to establish the optimal parameters for the analysis algorithm. We used the Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) method a strong Matlab contrast-enhancement method to outline better the physiological features of the scans. Parameters such as the contrast factor, the computed cumulative distribution function have been taken into consideration. The results are displayed graphically to enable any physician an accurate interpretation of the algorithm's performances.

Author Keywords: Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization algorithm

articleTitle: Effect of Multilayer Windings in Axial Motion Inductive Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This study examines the impact of multilayer windings on inductive power transfer in a rotating system. The 20-turn windings on the primary and secondary sides are modeled as single, double, and four-layer configurations, with identical air gaps, identical conductor spacings, and identical conductor counts. The configurations were evaluated based on power transfer efficiency under a 96V source voltage and a 100 kHz resonant frequency, using self-inductance and mutual inductance values derived from the models.

articleTitle: Architecture and Design Choices for an AI-enabled FPGA-based Cosmic Radiation Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) devices can be reconfigured after their manufacture to accelerate tasks such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) inference, provide lower response times and in some cases even lower power consumption compared to the software equivalent running on a modern microprocessor due to the capability of accessing their resources in parallel. Complex physics experiments and Space applications benefit greatly from FPGAs. We propose using a general-purpose, low-power, low-cost FPGA device in a nanosatellite as a cosmic radiation sensor. The AI-based hardware Cosmic Radiation Sensor (AICoRS) will be able to detect single event upsets (SEUs) and analyze the radiation patterns on the fly. The AICoRS system will be radiation tolerant to ensure correct operation in space conditions while acting as a SEU detector. We present the proposed architecture and the design choices we face, as well as a preliminary study of implementing the SEU detection element for evaluating the feasibility of using such a device for Space applications and for measuring cosmic radiation from the point of view of power consumption.

articleTitle: A Buck-Boost Converter with Coupled Inductors for High Voltage Boosting Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel high static conversion ratio buck-boost converter topology that employs coupled inductors to significantly increase the voltage boosting capability. The unique characteristics of the converter are explored for different values of the turns ratio, yielding to an asymmetrical static conversion ratio. A theoretical analysis of the proposed converter, together with a comparison of the static conversion ratio for multiple turns ratio values, the theoretical waveforms, design equations and the simulation results are provided in the paper. The results validate the potential of this topology to achieve a higher voltage gain. The converter proves its suitability for applications that require a high difference between input and output voltages.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of AI-Generated Text Using LLM Embedding-Driven ML Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLM) have proved their ability in tasks once thought to be exclusive to humans, such as text sumarization, completion, question answering, and others. Although LLMs were present for some time, OpenAI's ChatGPT introduced them to a broader audience. Despite their ability to assist humans in various tasks, some concerns arise, as there is a big probability of misuse in areas such as fake news, plagiarism, and propaganda. Previous studies have shown that humans are unable to accurately detect generated text, which motivates the need for automated detectors. In this work, we explore whether machine learning models can distinguish between text written by humans and generated text when using embeddings as input. We process a publicly available data set, Human ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (HC3). The data set contains question-answer pairs in various domains, including open-domain, financial, medical, legal, and psychological areas. We are using Llama3, an open-source large language model, to generate the embeddings. We then evaluate the performance of four machine learning (ML) models in detecting text generated by ChatGPT with the text embeddings used as input. The ML models are the Support Vector Classifier, Naive Bayes, the K-Nearest Neighbors Classifier, and a neural network. The results show that relatively simple models can identify the generated text. SVC demonstrated the best results with an F1-score of 99.95%.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Diagnosis for Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Using a Small Hybrid Transformer Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The Transformer Neural Network (TNN) architecture has emerged as a principal candidate in various data processing applications. Unlike traditional convolutional and recurrent Deep Neural Network (DNN) models, Transformers leverage a self-attention mechanism, allowing them to capture complex dependencies and relationships within data more effectively. This capability has enabled Transformers to consistently achieve superior performance across a wide range of tasks. Consequently, TNNs have become the architecture of choice for state-of-the-art models in both research and industry. This research aims to enhance AI-based automated diagnosis in medicine by exploring the small Hybrid Transformer Neural Network (HTNN) architecture for characterizing focal liver lesions (FLL) in contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) imagery. Our study initially reviewed recent TNN architectures employed in image classification tasks, followed by the identification of a suitable TNN variant for the aforementioned topic. This aim is supported by the fact that TNNs generally perform better with large training datasets, which is lacking in most medical datasets, including the one used in this study. We compared our approach with other machine learning solutions presented in the literature and found it achieves comparable accuracy. Additionally, our approach classifies more FLL types than most previous CEUS Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems.

articleTitle: Hydrological Sensing via FMCW Radar Technology of Sea Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Evaluating water dynamics, e.g., in near shore regions, is very important for an effective coastal monitoring. This paper introduces a methodology leveraging a cost-effective Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar system for sea wave assessment. This approach offers a dependable mechanism to acquire essential insights into wave attributes in coastal areas. Experimental assessments are considered to preliminarily assess the suitability of the approach, demonstrating the capacity of the employed short-range radar to provide meaningful insights into coastal sea states.

articleTitle: Dehazing CNNs Loss Functions Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper examines the performance of several loss functions in the context of image dehazing. We considered two CNN architectures for dehazing (AOD-Net and UVM-Net), trained on nine loss functions: L2, L1, Smooth L1, Huber, PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, HaarPSI, and PSNR-HVS. The latter two functions have not been previously used as loss functions, only for approximating human perceptions in various image processing tasks. The resulting 18 CNN models were tested on three different image dehazing datasets. Our results demonstrate that the perceptual loss functions (PSNR-HVS and HaarPSI) outperform the traditional loss functions for the CNN image dehazing models considered.

articleTitle: Using YOLOv9 Deep Learning Model for Automatic Detection and Classification of VHF Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The present work aims to highlight the results of using a convolutional neural network algorithm, namely You Only Look Once (YOLO) v9 in classification of very high frequency (VHF) emissions based on spectrograms recognition. A low-cost software-defined radio (SDR) transceiver with as low as 8 bits conversion capability was used to record four different types of VHF signals. Images of the spectrograms were used for training, validation, and testing of the dataset. The correct classification percentages were very good for all four classes of investigated radio emissions, with an average of 83.4%, even if the number of spectrograms per emission type used for training was as low as 150 and for validation 30. In these conditions, it resulted that YOLOv9 proves excellent capabilities in identification and classification of VHF signals received by low-resolution, low sensitivity, limited dynamic range and reduced spectrogram accuracy provided by the cheap SDR platform.

articleTitle: Characterizing Coastal Wave Energy Dynamics Using Enhanced FMCW Radar Signal Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Accurately characterizing wave energy dynamics in coastal regions is critical for applications ranging from renewable energy assessment to coastal safety and environmental monitoring. This paper introduces an advanced methodology that leverages Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar technology, enhanced by sophisticated signal processing techniques, to analyze and quantify wave energy in near-shore environments. By focusing on the normalized power spectrum, we explore how different wave conditions influence the distribution of energy across various frequencies. Our approach involves a comparative analysis of multiple signal processing methods, including Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), to enhance the accuracy and resolution of wave energy measurements. Experimental results from field tests conducted in coastal areas demonstrate the effectiveness of these techniques, revealing significant improvements in the radar's ability to capture detailed wave dynamics. The findings underscore the potential of this enhanced FMCW radar system as a reliable and cost-effective tool for real-time coastal monitoring, offering valuable insights for applications such as renewable energy forecasting and the protection of coastal infrastructure. This study contributes to the growing body of research on non-contact hydrological sensing, highlighting the critical role of signal processing in advancing the precision and utility of radar-based wave energy assessments.

articleTitle: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Transformer Attention for Low-Light Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning, particularly in Transformer architectures, have revolutionized tasks that require processing complex, highly-detailed data. One such task is low-light image enhancement, a critical sub-field of image restoration, which has benefited from extensive research into various Transformer models, each offering distinct strengths. This paper introduces a novel Transformer attention mechanism inspired by the Kolmogorov - Arnold representation theorem, leveraging learnable non-linearity and multivariate function de-composition. This attention mechanism is utilized to develop KAN - T, our Transformer network. These enhancements enable greater feature flexibility and broader context capture within the model. Our comprehensive experiments, both quantitative and qualitative, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in low-light image enhancement, highlighting its effectiveness and wide-ranging applicability.

articleTitle: Fostering Trust in AI-Driven Healthcare: A Brief Review of Ethical and Practical Considerations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to become more integrated into healthcare systems, establishing trust is crucial for its successful implementation and widespread use. This paper examines the ethical and practical considerations necessary for cultivating trust in AI-driven healthcare. It begins by exploring the ethical challenges that can erode patient and provider confidence in AI, such as concerns about data privacy, informed consent, and algorithmic bias. The discussion then moves to the importance of transparency in AI systems, emphasizing the need for explainable AI models that enable healthcare professionals to understand and interpret AI-driven recommendations effectively. Additionally, the paper highlights the vital role of accountability and governance frameworks to ensure that AI applications comply with ethical standards and regulations. It also considers practical aspects, including the implementation of strong data management practices, ongoing monitoring of AI system performance, and the participation of multidisciplinary teams in the development and deployment of AI solutions. By addressing these ethical and practical issues, this paper aims to offer a strategic approach for building trust in AI-driven healthcare, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes, improved care delivery, and a more ethical application of advanced technologies within the health sector.

articleTitle: Innovative Pixel Art: Generation and Augmentation with Pixray
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The recent surge in the popularity of indie games has highlighted a growing trend towards pixel art as a favoured approach. Simultaneously, advancements in artificial intelligence have enabled the development of tools that can generate, modify, and enhance images, opening new possibilities for game art creation. This paper explores the intersection of these trends by examining the use of state-of-the-art AI tools to generate and augment pixel art. The objective is to identify a set of practical, accessible AI tools that can assist game developers in the creative process, from concept art to in-game assets. By evaluating the effectiveness, ease of use, and quality of outputs produced by various AI models, this study aims to provide actionable insights into how these technologies can streamline the art development pipeline in indie game creation. The findings aim to empower developers, regardless of their artistic skill level, to leverage AI-driven methods for enhancing their game's visual appeal and creative process.

articleTitle: Data Prediction Algorithms in Real-Time Using Internet of Things and Named-Data Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Current paper presents a new perspective on Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) data processing. There are three aspects considered herein: data management, data security and post-processing using Machine Learning (ML). The model was used to predict values which can be useful indicators for remote patient monitoring or athlete performance tracking. We selected FIWARE platform for data management. The security layer was resolved using a proxy server and authentication methods for both sensors and users, whilst Named-Data Networks (NDN) was needed for external communication. Data prediction was offered by Deep Echo State Networks (DESN), which offers good performance in terms of RMSE, training time and prediction time. For experiments, the WESAD dataset used different measurements collected over a longer period from different body sensors (temperature, blood pressure, EKG). The proposed approach is a suitable alternative for data management using the API developed by us, while NDN secures data retrieval from outside the platform.

articleTitle: Smoke Detection Using an Optical Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved solution for the use of optical sensors for smoke detection with digital output. It will be part of a digital system employing a microcontroller. These systems often produce better results than their analog counterparts, having better detection accuracy. The data are transmitted through a communication protocol, SPI, and the microcontroller will initiate a phone call by a GSM module. The architecture, detailed hardware design, and software development, together with PCB artwork, are disclosed.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security in Data Exchange: Mitigating Risks Solutions in Base64 Encoding and JSON Web Tokens
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper evaluates the relationship between Base64 encoding and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) in the context of authentication and authorization and proposes solutions for reducing security risks. JWTs, commonly used for secure data exchange as JSON objects, utilize Base64 encoding to ensure safe transmission. Analyzing Base64's impact on JWT tokens enhances our comprehension of securing sensitive data and enabling secure user sessions, while also addressing related risks. In our research, besides analyzing the interplay between Base64 encoding and JWTs we also propose effective measures to mitigate the risks involved. By addressing these vulnerabilities head-on, we enhance the security of sensitive data and foster secure user sessions. This research enhances secure token handling by adopting robust cryptographic standards, ensuring the confidentiality of signing secrets and employing JSON Web Encryption (JWE) to shield payloads from interception, thereby addressing gaps and enhancing security measures beyond existing literature.

articleTitle: Hybrid Implementation of a Doppler Shift Compensation Solution for LEO Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The relative movements between a satellite in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and its ground station lead to rapid variations in Doppler shift, which influence the quality of communications and the acquisition of telemetry data. Understanding and compensating for this lag is crucial to maintaining the quality and accuracy of communication links. This article outlines the development of a generalized solution that combining both hardware and software components to efficiently estimate and correct this Doppler shift for LEO satellites by considering transmission delays as well as satellite ephemeris data. This approach was implemented in a processing board integrated into an S-band ground station located in Algeria. The experimental results obtained during real passes of the ALSAT-2A satellite were satisfactory, and the Doppler compensation model offered precision correlated to the estimated Doppler frequency.

articleTitle: Particle Filter Based Correction of On-Board Camera Driver Gaze Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Gaze estimation is an important tool for implementing driver assistance and autonomous driving algorithms. The accuracy of the estimation is crucial considering the impact of failure of such algorithms. In the last decade, an important effort was made to increase this accuracy. However, there are some dynamic conditions that have a great impact on it such as camera vibration determined by road holes or bumps, driver eyes blink or light reflections. The work presented in this paper proposes a modular solution designed to increase the accuracy of gaze prediction independently by the estimation method. It consists of a post-processing step involving a particle filtering solution meant to correct dynamic errors appearing under harsh conditions. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we use in the validation step an implementation of gaze estimation based on efficient L2CS-Net architecture followed by the particle filter correction module implemented in Python. The test results demonstrate the performance of the presented solution.

articleTitle: Simulating Human Physical Behavior using Unreal Engine Full Body Inverse Kinematics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Extracting, analyzing, and simulating human physical behavior have proven to be challenging tasks for researchers all over the world for many years. If developed successfully, they can generate important results that will contribute to progress in many fields. These results can change many people's lives, aiding in a handful of domains, such as security, medicine, autonomous robots, and many more. A direct outcome is to obtain the data necessary to train and validate advanced neural network models implied by many of today's solutions. We propose here an approach that uses Unreal Engine 5 to reproduce the movements characteristic to normal human behavior in a simulated environment, considering restrictions of body joints. This method can be used to aid in creating flawless body animation, both procedural and AI generated. It can be included in healthcare-related body simulations, video game development, and in some other fields involving research on physical human or animal behavior.

articleTitle: Are Vegetation Indices Really so Different: An Unsupervised Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Remote sensing has been employed to gather rapidly dynamic, nondestructive information on crops and has been utilized across numerous fields. The information richness has been condensed into a plurality of vegetation indices. They offer quantitative data about crop growth and health, supporting a range of precision agriculture practices. The introduction of many indices has been motivated by particular problems unsolved by the previous list. In this paper we investigate if these indices are indeed so different and to quantify the differences among them we assume an unsupervised approach. We focus our study on a PRISMA image from Brasov area. Out of this image, we select four semantic areas indicating agricultural crop, forest, alpine pasture and urban setting and into these four cases we evaluate differences between the most used vegetation index, NDVI, and other several popular choices. The differences are quantified from a statistic viewpoint, using Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients and from an image consistency, using SSIM. We show that conditioned on semantic category, significant differences arise.

articleTitle: A Python-Based Real Estate Rental Application for Students: Leveraging Open Data and Visualization to Enhance Housing Decisions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The growing demand for accessible and affordable housing for students has highlighted the need for innovative solutions in real estate applications tailored to the academic community. This paper presents a student-led approach in the development of a real-estate renting app specifically designed for current or future students who plan to study at universities in Timisoara. The app prototype utilizes Python and open-source technologies to create a user-friendly platform that simplifies the process of finding suitable rental options. By addressing key challenges faced by students-such as affordability, location proximity to campuses, and ease of use-the prototype offers a cost-effective solution for student housing. This work establishes a practical model for future innovations in student-focused real estate applications, showcasing how a collaborative, frugal approach can drive impactful technology development.

articleTitle: Teach to Reach Younger Students by “Electronics”
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of learning Electronics efficiently among first-year Computer Science students. It originates in the identification of an initial fear related to circuits and hardware, fueled by the lack of skills in this field. Based on the advantage given by the fact that students are at an age of great receptivity and like to be stimulated, we adopt methods that train thinking, by promoting active learning, increasing optimal motivation, and facilitating the sequence of the learning phases. The results show a favorable response of the students to this type of approach.

articleTitle: Ultra-compact Implantable MIMO Antenna with Radiation Pattern Diversity for Scalp-based Implants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This work presents the development of a new ultra-compact implantable two-element MIMO antenna with radiation diversity for bio-telemetry communication in scalp-based implants. The design consists of two separated mirrored semicircular slotted patches that radiate in dissimilar directions to enable radiation diversity. The proposed antenna occupies a very compact volume of 4.085 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>and is designed to resonate at 2.4 GHz. Two different numerical techniques were used to validate the antenna's performance in a scalp-based environment. Due to symmetry, both antenna's radiating elements achieved a fractional bandwidth of 25.13% and a peak gain of -19.8 dBi at the resonance frequency. The antenna showed an ability to radiate in two dissimilar directions with a radiation coverage angle of ± 60°. Specific absorption rate and link budget analyses were conducted and demonstrated the antenna's ability to perform bio-telemetry communication at high data rates of up to 100 Mbps while satisfying power safety regulations.

articleTitle: NTN Agent for System Information Block SIB19
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: 3GPP Release 17 introduces Non-Terrestrial Network as a fundamental part of the actual 5G and future 6G mobile networks. The paper focus on one of the problem encountered in 5G NTN implementation: the large delay induced by the satellites. To overcome this problem, 3GPP proposes a new System Information Block SIB19 to be added, carrying all the necessary information on the timing and satellite orbital parameters to address all the satellite specific challenges. Considering the importance of the in-lab testing prior to over the satellite testing, we use Open Air Interface (OAI), an open source implementation of 5G NTN protocol stack, together with our in-house satellite channel emulator to build an end-to-end testing setup for 5G NTN over LEO/MEO/GEO satellites. A new module that implements SIB19 in OAI software is proposed and validated with the OAI community. In the same time we consider to use Two Line Element as satellite orbital parameters descriptor to derive all necessary parameters for both channel emulator and the new SIB19 module. This way we provide a perfect synchronization between 5G platform and channel emulator for LEO/MEO satellites. The success of the proposed setup and SIB19 implementation was confirmed by experiments.

articleTitle: Validation of Real-world Measurements Through Ray Tracing Simulation for 5G Urban Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to validate ray tracing simulations using real-world measurements in 5G urban scenarios. The measurements were obtained by traversing specific routes and recording parameters such as position, Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR), Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP), and Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ) using the Quectel RM500Q 5G module as user equipment (UE). Subsequently, these real-world measurements are used to validate a MATLAB-based ray tracing simulation. Simulating such scenarios in a controlled environment allows for easy manipulation and study of various parameters, enabling compre-hensive verification of the simulator's accuracy. The advantage of this approach lies in its ability to ensure the reliability of the simulation tool, enabling robust testing of diverse scenarios and parameters for deployments in real-world use cases.

articleTitle: The Automation of the Verification Process of Hardware IP Registers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The technology progress witnessed in the past few decades would have not been possible without the hardware support, which nowadays is most of the time a System on Chip (SoC) composed of multiple Hardware Intellectual Properties (IPs). The SoC market faces a number of challenges, including among them the time required to bring a concept to market availability. Frequently, this challenge is handled by developing configurable IPs, which can have their configurations changed depending on the requirements. Because the configurability is achieved predominantly through registers, the number of registers inside the IP and the complexity of the verification process escalate with the number of configurations. The Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) offers the UVM Register Abstraction Layer (UVM RAL) library for the management and the access of the registers, which has a series of benefits that are accompanied by the cost of its development. This paper addresses the automation of the UVM RAL generation with the help of a Python script that accepts as input a file in xlsx format with the registers description and generates the UVM register model. The register model has been integrated in a verification environment alongside the Device under Test (DUT) for which it was generated, in order to validate the functionality of the script.

articleTitle: An Overview of GaN Technology for Power Conversion Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The growing demand for electric vehicles, renewable energy, and portable electronics has increased the prevalence of power conversion systems (PCS), as exemplified by the architecture of electric automobiles. Research and development in semiconductor technologies aim to achieve reduced system size and higher efficiency in these power conversion applications (PCA). Gallium Nitride (GaN) Wide Bandgap (WBG) technology has proven to be a competitive choice for these requirements. This paper presents how different milestones of this technology have benefited the field. For instance, using GaN technology can increase the delivered power by 37.5% while achieving an efficiency of 99% in the case of a synchronous boost converter. Additionally, it has enabled new converter topologies with a power density of 123.3 kW/L and an efficiency of 90.9%.

articleTitle: FuzzWiz - Fuzzing Framework for Efficient Hardware Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Ever-increasing design complexity of System-on-Chips (SoCs) led to significant verification challenges. Unlike software, bugs in hardware design are vigorous and eternal i.e., once the hardware is fabricated, it cannot be repaired with any patch. Despite being one of the powerful techniques used in verification, the dynamic random approach cannot give confidence to complex Register Transfer Level (RTL) designs during the pre-silicon design phase. In particular, achieving coverage targets and exposing bugs is a complicated task with random simulations. In this paper, we leverage an existing testing solution available in the software world known as fuzzing and apply it to hardware verification in order to achieve coverage targets in quick time. We created an automated hardware fuzzing framework FuzzWiz using metamodeling and Python to achieve coverage goals faster. It includes parsing the RTL design module, converting it into C/C++ models, creating generic testbench with assertions, fuzzer-specific compilation, linking, and fuzzing. Furthermore, it is configurable and provides the debug flow if any crash is detected during the fuzzing process. The proposed framework is applied on four IP blocks from Google's OpenTitan chip with various fuzzing engines to show its scalability and compatibility. Our benchmarking results show that we could achieve around 90 % of the coverage 10 times faster than traditional simulation regression based approach.

articleTitle: Early Identification of Potato Fields using Data Fusion and Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose an approach for the preseason identi-fication of potato fields using a fused dataset that consists of a multispectral image from Sentinel-2 and a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image from Sentinel-1 satellite. Ground truth data is provided by the National Institute of Potato and Sugar Beet, Brasov, Romania. Both images were acquired on the 23<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> of May 2023, when the characteristic ridges were prepared during the potato seeding. We processed and visualized the temporal data using all the available SAR Ground Range Detected images in 2023 to observe the changes. Further, we aligned the pixels from multispectral and SAR images and created vectors that represent the fused data points where each vector has five values representing features in the dataset. The final dataset has 5233 vectors which are further used to train and test an artificial neural network (ANN) with two hidden layers and it performs binary classification of potato and non-potato fields. As a result, a training accuracy of 94.41% and a test accuracy of 93.03% were achieved. We compared this with results from the crop growth season (96.88% accuracy), noting the increased contribution of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) during this period compared to bare soil classification.

articleTitle: Intelligent Plant Monitoring and Care System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Domotics, as a complex field with many possible applications, stimulates the creativity of large teams of professionals worldwide. Every day new applications and systems are being created in home automation area, giving people more control over their smart homes and providing them with a detailed status about appliances' activity. Aligning to this trend, this article describes the realisation of a modern complex electronic system that, using an internet connection, allows houseplant owners to care for and monitor their flowers when they are out of their home for several days. It is demonstrated that, using an regular Arduino board connected to a few low-cost peripherals and creating a framework employing some of the most common programming languages, a stable and easy-to-use system in domotics domain has been created. The details on the programming flow, the components used and the code provided in this paper can help any electronics enthusiast to build its own electronic system for plant care or similar activities.

articleTitle: Enhancing Audio Performance: Noise Reduction and Efficiency in Class AB Amplifier Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and optimization of a Class AB Audio Amplifier aimed at high-fidelity applications. A simple and compact Hi-Fi audio amplifier was designed with features to improve the audio quality (power supply regulator, digital volume control, low-frequency driver pre-amplifier, VU meter on display). Key performance specifications such as bandwidth, total harmonic distortion (THD), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and output power are thoroughly analyzed to ensure superior audio quality. The study addresses various noise sources, including intrinsic component noise, power supply interference, and inter-stage interference. Advanced techniques to minimize noise and enhance the Power Supply Rejection Ratio (PSRR) are discussed, as well as the usage of high-capacity smoothing capacitors and discrete voltage regulators. The layout design is planned to prevent crosstalk and electromagnetic coupling. Furthermore, the power supply design, incorporating efficient transformers and smoothing capacitors, is optimized for reduced energy consumption and improved PSRR.

articleTitle: 3D Urban Wireless Network Planning and Analysis Using Ray-Tracing and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: ReliableWi-Fi coverage is essential for the functioning of IoT devices in smart cities. This study utilizes advanced Ray-Tracing techniques and Machine Learning to enhance Wi-Fi signal coverage across a university campus. We analyze a comprehensive dataset comprising measurements from three Wi-Fi frequencies (2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz) and five ray-tracing configurations (0/0, 0/1, 1/0, 1/1, and 2/1), along with two power levels (100mW and 200mW) and a 5-meter resolution grid featuring 3,135 receivers, resulting in a total of 94,050 rows and 28 columns, amounting to 2,633,400 data points. The Random Forest Regressor Model demonstrates strong predictive capabilities, as evidenced by low error metrics (Mean Absolute Error of 1.44 dBm, Mean Squared Error of 6.46, and R-squared of 0.99), validating its effectiveness for accurate signal strength estimations. Furthermore, feature importance analysis highlights the significance of link status and signal coverage in prediction accuracy, underscoring the necessity for effective feature selection. This research provides valuable insights for optimizing Wi-Fi network planning in urban environments, establishing a solid foundation for future investigations.

articleTitle: Revisiting Mixing Transformations and Chaotic Systems with a View to Cryptographic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper extends the study of the construction of mixing transformations with chaotic systems regarding the influence of the control parameters in image-based cryptographic applications. An improved mixing function which increases the level of diffusion and confusion in the encrypted image for different values of the control parameters is proposed. The advantage of this construction is obtaining a more complex encryption scheme by offering the possibility of expanding the key space. The chaotic systems chosen for the construction of the mixing function are the well-known logistic map and Hénon map, but other dynamic systems can also be used.

articleTitle: Synthetic Radar Data Generation from RGB Images for Robotics and Autonomous Driving Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose a novel approach to enhance the re-liability of autonomous driving systems through the generation of synthetic Range-Azimuth (RA) heatmaps from RGB images. The method involves the generation of synthetic Range-Azimuth (RA) heatmaps from RGB images or relative depth images, facilitating the extraction of essential depth and azimuth angle information through supervised learning. This effectively bridges the gap between visual and radar data modalities, offering a more comprehensive and context-aware approach to mitigate noise and enhance the quality of radar-based perception. In summary, our method leverages a GAN-based architecture with tailored loss functions. These tailored loss functions play a pivotal role in refining the accuracy and realism of the generated heatmaps, ensuring a more robust and reliable perception system for autonomous driving. Our approach also highlights the potential for data augmentation, enabling synthetic data generation for non-existent or safety-critical scenarios. Additionally, our method serves as a secondary system, providing redundancy in situations where radar systems may fail, like degraded or cluttered reflections, enhancing the overall safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems. We demonstrate the results of the proposed methodology on benchmark datasets (CRUW) in comparison with SOTA methods using appropriate quantitative and qualitative metrics.

articleTitle: ALPHA-EDU: An Educational Platform for Alphabet Learning with AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In contemporary society, children have become accustomed to acquiring information through images and their learning is often enhanced by the use of visual aids in education. This article presents an educational computer application designed for preschool children to assist in learning the letters of the Latin alphabet. Given the benefits of incorporating the concept of gamification into the educational process, a fun and engaging game was created to help students make visual associations between letters and animal images. Using the application, which is based on convolutional neural networks, children draw letters by connecting dots on the screen, can move from one level of the application to another and thus learn animal names more easily. By utilizing various programming languages, effectively training a model for letter recognition and developing an intuitive graphical user interface, it has been demonstrated that a practical and engaging application has been created, which has been well-received by children.

articleTitle: Improving the Elective Courses Selection Process by Extending an Educational Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: An essential and sometimes overlooked part of the educational process consists of the administrative procedures that need to take place for learning to occur smoothly. One such procedure is the selection of elective courses that some students need to complete, according to their corresponding curriculum. Moodle, the leading open-source Learning Management System, does not provide an adequate tool for directly facilitating this process. The purpose of this student-lead research was to design, build and test such a system. The results of the research, presented here and in a final diploma project, are encouraging and provide the starting point for an effective tool to manage the whole elective courses selection process.

articleTitle: DepthLux: Depthwise Separable Convolution Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Low-light image enhancement is a critical task in computer vision, often challenged by noise, low contrast, and color distortion. Traditional convolutional neural networks rely heavily on normal convolutions, which can be computationally intensive and less efficient in handling spatial dependencies in low light conditions. We propose a novel transformer-based framework for low-light image enhancement that eschews nor-mal convolutions in favor of depthwise separable convolutions. Experimental results demonstrate that our method matches the performance of state-of-the-art methods by adopting a novel approach for the feed forward network, which typically uses linear and convolutional filters that increase computational cost. This approach presents a promising direction for efficient and effective low-light image enhancement in real-world applications.

articleTitle: GLCM-Enhanced Dynamic Texture Analysis for Ocean Waves Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper advances an analysis of ocean waves showcasing a combination between 3D approaches of dynamic textures and time variations of co-occurrence matrix features, viewed as a new dimension. The main features deployed in the present work are: contrast, homogeneity, correlation, directivity and entropy calculated for following directions, i.e. front to back, left to right, top to bottom and 3D spatial translations. The method provides a genuinely effective tool for spatio-temporal analysis of dynamic textures. The approach based on dynamic textures are applied on ocean waves from the DynTex database.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Phishing URL Detection Using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Phishing is one of the most common attacks in the field of cybersecurity. Different Machine Learning and Artificial Neural Network techniques were used to detect phishing URLs. We used three datasets with different features and we implemented three Machine learning algorithms (Decision Trees, Random Forests and XGBoost) and three Artificial Neural Network algorithms (MLS, CNN and LSTM). The results we obtained demonstrate that XGBoost and Random Forests have the best performance and a low training time compared to the other candidates.

articleTitle: Permissioned Blockchain-as-a-Service: Architecting Secure and Efficient Private Blockchain Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Public distributed ledger systems often fall short for corporate use due to limited transaction processing capabilities, high costs, suboptimal consensus mechanisms, and inadequate data protection. As demand for advanced transaction-oriented analysis grows, distributed ledger technologies have gained attention across various sectors, driving the development of diverse blockchain architectures. This article examines the Hyperledger Fabric framework, focusing on its deployment using local command-line interfaces, architecture, and transaction mechanisms. Our proof of concept demonstrates the creation of resilient, scalable blockchain networks by applying modern software principles to distributed ledgers. We break down Hyperledger Fabric into containerized microservices, orchestrated with Docker and Kubernetes, to enhance flexibility and scalability. The study evaluates the Hyperledger Fabric architecture, data handling within the ledger, and operational efficiency through a rigorous analysis of transactions per second (TPS), latency, and overall performance. These metrics are assessed in a setup that closely emulates real-world scenarios, with multiple organizations participating in the distributed ledger system. This provides insights into the framework's viability for enterprise blockchain solutions.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Steganography Detection in Media Files
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This article entails the analysis of different steganography algorithms, including LSB and DCT. The innovation of this work consisted in the construction of a dataset and the implementation of a stego image classification system using deep learning techniques, such as GoogleNet, AlexNet and ResNet. Experimental results demonstrate the performance of different CNN architectures in detecting modified images and the type of steganographic algorithm used.

Index Terms: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Cooperative Transportation Systems using the V2X-based MOSAIC Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Rapid urban growth and increased vehicle use present major challenges for traditional transportation systems, causing congestion, accidents, and pollution. Traffic jams lead to delays, economic losses, and accidents. This study explores the V2X-based MOSAIC platform for traffic data analysis in Iasi, Romania's second-largest city, assessing indicators like density and speed. The aim is to enhance efficiency and safety in urban transport, offering insights to reduce congestion with future intelligent systems.

articleTitle: Audiosusceptibility Calculation in One-Cycle Controlled DC-DC Converters Based on the Describing Function
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Audiosusceptibility of a buck converter employing on-cycle control is investigated using the describing function method. First, the one-cycle control principle is presented and then the describing function method is briefly discussed. The describing function method is applied to a one-cycle controlled buck converter in order to derive the audiosusceptibility transfer function. The procedure is implemented in Matlab and then the Caspoc simulations validated the correctness of the theoretical considerations. The results provided in Caspoc simulation, both for the magnitude and phase characteristics, overimposed with good accuracy on the Bode diagrams calculated in Matlab, and therefore an excellent match between the two diagrams is observed. The existence of a critical frequency where a perturbation in the input voltage is least attenuated is revealed and has to be considered in converter design.

articleTitle: An Innovative Solution with Wearable and Aboard-the-Vehicle Sensors Integrated with Machine Learning Algorithms for Monitoring the Driver's Psycho-Physical Condition for Safety Purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Recent progress in automotive safety has led to the development of an intelligent multi-sensor system for monitoring driver stress and fatigue. Monitoring the driver's psycho-physical state helps reduce risks to drivers and pedestrians. A literature review has been conducted on existing systems for detecting bio-signals and their use in evaluating the driver's psycho-physical condition. This study proposes the architecture of a monitoring system to classify driver fatigue using wearable devices and in-vehicle sensors to detect physiological signals, vehicle dynamics data, and traffic and weather information accessed by the driver's smartphone. The system employs an ensemble learning strategy to enhance the accuracy of fatigue detection compared to classic video-based systems. This approach aims to improve road safety by enabling intervention before a loss of attention occurs.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis Combining Radio-over-Fiber and Power-over-Fiber with Distributed Amplification for Different Link Lengths
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A Power-over-Fiber (PoF) system provides a power supply, over an optical fiber, to a remote electrical equipment. A Radio over Fiber (RoF) system is basically the transmission of Radio Frequency signals (RF) over optical fiber. Combining PoF with RoF allows a fully photonic link to supply remote sensors, while transmitting RF signals. A single optical fiber is deployed to both transmit the exchanged data and the energy to supply the remote instrument. This work presents an overview of the optical and RF performances of a system that combines PoF and RoF with a focus on experimental results. It presents both advantages and limitations of this approach and should serve as a guide to which applications may benefit from the concept.

articleTitle: Radar Object Classification Using Neural Networks in Urban Automotive Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to solve the problem of object classification for automotive radar systems. This is done using neural networks and knowing attributes about the objects such as their trajectory, acceleration, velocity, velocity and acceleration standard deviation, object length and width and other parameters related to object's movement. The method proposed is validated by experiments, obtaining in process of validation an overall accuracy over 99%: for the pedestrian class an accuracy of 99.88%, for the cyclist class an accuracy of 99.23% and for the car class 99.82% accuracy.

articleTitle: A High-Speed, Area-Optimized, ROM-Less (Co)Sine Wave Synthesis Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Sine and cosine wave synthesis is utilized for generating sinusoidal-alike values in the digital domain. While this task is handled through software, dedicated hardware like Direct Digital Synthesis (DDS) is also available.
