However, both methods rely on memory resources, such as look-up tables and Read-Only Memories (ROMs), which face latency limitations related to additional memory access times on top of additional Si area. With the advent of real-time arithmetic for sine wave approximation, this paper presents an all-in-one digital module that employs iterative multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations for sine and cosine synthesis, ready to be integrated in Systems-on-Chip (SoCs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), or even standalone ASICs. Compared to ROM-less solutions like Taylor approximation, the proposed architecture achieves 80.80% lower resource utilization, 80.39% reduced propagation delay, and 36.66% higher accuracy in sine and cosine wave approximation, both operating as 32-bit systems with one sample per clock cycle.

articleTitle: Reduce Computational Complexity For Continuous Wavelet Transform in Acoustic Recognition Using Hop Size
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In recent years, the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) has been employed as a spectral feature extractor for acoustic recognition tasks in conjunction with machine learning and deep learning models. However, applying the CWT to each individual audio sample is computationally intensive. This paper proposes an approach that applies the CWT to a subset of samples, spaced according to a specified hop size. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly reduces computational costs while maintaining the robust performance of the trained models.

articleTitle: An Overview and Classification on Beamforming Techniques for 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: 5G technologies have opened a new chapter in the field of connectivity, offering superior speeds, reduced latency, and unprecedented opportunities for a variety of industries. One example is the use of beamforming in 5G systems. Beamforming is a technique that enhances the signal power for individual users and minimizes interference from other users, hence boosting the overall capacity. This paper provides an in-depth review of the classification of beamforming methods that are suitable for 5G systems. Another subject of discussion is beam management, which refers to a sequence of protocols at layers 1 and 2 that are used to create and sustain a set of connections between two beams.

articleTitle: Assessment of LPDDR4 Interface Performance in an Automotive Product Through High-Speed Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Automotive products require an accurate assessment of Signal Integrity (SI). This study proposes a solution for using high speed modeling tools to evaluate the SI efficiency of automotive items. Methods for managing SI simulations for a Low Power Double Data Rate 4 (LPDDR4) memory are presented. Due to its fast data transfer speeds and low power consumption, the design and use of the LPDDR4 memory needs to consider signal integrity.

articleTitle: Overview of the Technical Risk Analysis and Risk Assessment Analysis in Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The Automotive Industry is at a pivotal moment, transitioning from traditional vehicles to fully autonomous systems. To ensure the safety of autonomous vehicles, standards such as those from the ISO (International Organization for Standardization), IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission), and SAE (Society of Automotive Engineers) are enforced. However, to be effectively implemented, these standards must adapt to the evolving landscape of Level 4 (L4) autonomous systems. This adaptation requires the use of various Technical Risk Analyses and Technical Risk Assessments methods. The purpose of this paper is to identify the most used methods and provide a systematic overview, aiming to create a comprehensive understanding of the domain. We consider this systematic overview essential in such a dynamic and rapidly evolving environment.

articleTitle: TMBuD-v2: A Multi-Purpose Urban Landmark Detection Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Recognition and identification of urban landmarks is not a facile task and naturally blends several research topics like image signal processing, computer vision, augmented reality. In this paper we introduce TMBuD-v2 - Timişoara Building Dataset - a multi-purpose dataset for urban landmark recognition. The TMBuD-v2 building dataset contains 1360 images with the resolution of 768 × 1024 pixels taken using a mobile phone from a street view perspective. The images are organized into 144 district landmarks located in several tourist parts of Timisşoara. The proposed dataset offers the possibility of evaluating landmark recognition solutions in urban scenario, salient edges on the buildings, and semantic segmentation of the urban environment. The dataset is available at https://github.com/CipiOrhei/TMBuD

articleTitle: Integrated and Automated Intrusion Detection System: A Comprehensive Review of Current Challenges and Methods, Future Trends and Prospects for Emerging Electronics Engineering with AI Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The effectiveness of intrusion detection systems (IDS) is crucial for protecting assets and preventing unauthorized access. Advanced and Automated Intrusion Detection Systems are at the forefront of this domain, utilizing cutting-edge electronics engineering concepts and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) to boost detection precision and system reliability. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the challenges currently encountered by IDS, explores the latest trends in electronics engineering, and discusses the potential of AI to revolutionize intrusion detection. We also compare existing detection methods to highlight the impact of automated and integrated IDS on modern security challenges and advancements.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of DoA Estimation Using Multiple Choices OMP Algorithm in Conditions of Mutual Coupling Between Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This study provides a novel approach regarding direction of arrival (DoA) for an uniform linear array (ULA) antenna elements using Multiple Choices Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (MCOMP) in conditions of mutual coupling. This angle estimation technique presents a solution using single snapshot RADAR signal acquisition. The advantages of the proposed method are proved by numerical simulations for different order and amplitude of mutual coupling between antennas.

articleTitle: Textual Authenticity in the AI Era: Evaluating BERT and RoBERTa with Logistic Regression and Neural Networks for Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: AI-generated content impersonating human writing is an issue that has gained attention as AI spreads its wings. This particular study serves as a comparison between the existing Logistic Regression and Feedforward Neural Networks (FNNs) by employing sentence-BERT-appended models and RoBERTa in the determination of authenticity in a given text. A dataset that was balanced between human-written and AI-generated texts was utilized. Techniques like tokenization and normalization were first used, followed by feature extraction using transformer-based models. Cross-validation and confusion matrix analysis that used measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and ROC AUC were included to guarantee the models’ robustness. The hybrid RoBERTa-FNN model that was deposed challengers was the most outstanding model in respect of precision and recall, and the highest accuracy (99.95%) was obtained as mentioned in the data. The improved performance serves as a proof of how effectively RoBERTa uses its embeddings to represent context on the fine-grained level required for this kind of text classification. This work is a stepping stone to the creation of strong AI text detection systems, besides our advancements to the knowledge of models and embedding performance with respect to text classification. The results lay emphasis on the selection of model configuration and the embedding technique, as they are the key factors in achieving the best results in practical applications.

articleTitle: An Architecture of a Web Application for Deploying Machine Learning Models in Healthcare Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: An important gap exists between advanced Deep Learning (DL) models developed for medical imaging and their insitu implementation in clinical environments. Our research proposes a scalable software architecture for a web-based computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) application that bridges the gap between research and production. The main goals are: (1) creating an intuitive interface for non-technical users and, (2) designating a feedback mechanism to enhance the Machine Learning (ML) models with medical expertise. The architecture assumes a microservices approach, containerization, and current web technologies to enable seamless deployment and user-friendliness. Key components include ONNX-based model conversion for cross- platform compatibility, asynchronous processing based on FastAPI, and a modular data handling system using PostgreSQL. Our proof-of-concept (PoC) shows the system's feasibility by deploying it on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and getting initial feedback from clinicians. Early findings indicate potential improvements in model usability and stakeholder engagement. Future actions will involve implementing continuous integration and delivery pipelines to improve system resilience and scalability.

articleTitle: Educational Matlab Tool for Evaluating Liver Tumors Using Ultrasound
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a Matlab application for computer-assisted learning in the evaluation of liver tumors using ultrasound. Diagnosing liver tumors detected during standard ultrasound exams is challenging for doctors, often requiring detailed investigations for accurate diagnosis and effective treatment. Computerized analysis of ultrasound images can significantly aid doctors in interpreting these images and formulating accurate diagnoses. The Matlab programming environment provides various tools for processing biomedical images. In this study, Histogram and Entropy functions were utilized to accurately differentiate between malignant and benign liver tumors. Additionally, Matlab App Designer was used to create a user-friendly interface for doctors. This application is also beneficial for students, offering a valuable tool for self-testing and skill development in clinical ultrasound courses and practical sessions. The proposed Matlab application employs classic image processing tools and serves as useful software for students learning liver ultrasound techniques.

articleTitle: A Quality-Improving Method for APT-Type NOAA Meteorological Satellite Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The Automatic Picture Transmission (APT) analog technology is still utilized on certain weather satellites, such as the NOAA polar-orbiting satellites, to transmit weather images in visible and infrared light. Like any satellite transmission, the APT transmission is influenced by the considerable distance between the satellite and the receiver, as well as the shadowing caused by the surroundings. Due to these factors, the SNR of the received signal may be low, necessitating the use of denoising techniques to enhance the quality of the decoded image. The paper proposes a denoising solution based on a smoothing technique, which is implemented at the demodulation process level, unlike other solutions that process the decoded image. Computer simulations were conducted to showcase the efficacy of the proposed solution. The simulations demonstrated that even a simple moving-average-based smoothing technique yields excellent results, making the solution suitable for basic APT receivers.

articleTitle: Sensor Data Analysis in a Real-Time IoT and Blockchain-Based System for Monitoring Driver Alcohol Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Monitoring alcohol levels of drivers is essential for maintaining public safety, especially for preventing traffic accidents. This paper presents the development and evaluation of a sensor-based module designed to predict breath alcohol levels using a modular sensor battery, integrated with blockchain technology and a data collection platform. The proposed system monitors the driver's location and alcohol level in real-time, preserving data integrity through the use of blockchain. The experimental setup involved varying alcohol concentrations and measuring sensor responses at different distances from the source. The core of this research is the analysis of the collected data, using machine learning techniques, specifically Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting, to assess the reliability and accuracy of the sensor readings. The analysis confirmed a strong correlation between the sensor's readings and actual alcohol levels, demonstrating that the system achieves high accuracy when the sensors are placed within 1000 mm of the source.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Sleep Staging Using EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Sleep plays a crucial role in the physical and mental health of an individual. The importance of sleep in the well-being of an individual is widely recognized, and so are the effects of the sleep disorders or disturbances. These sleep disorders, for example insomnia or sleep apnea, affect the individual's sleep structure and quality, and are worrisomely prevalent across all age and sex categories. There exists a substantial body of literature which indicates that sleep disturbances can severely reduce the quality of life and, additionally, present themselves as risk factors in the development of other health or psychological disorders, such as cardiovascular disease or depression. Sleep staging, the classification of the stages of sleep, is a valuable tool in the detection of sleep disorders such as insomnia. This paper proposes a Deep Learning-based method for sleep staging, using single-channel EEG data. A CNN-LSTM Deep Neural Network is used. The paper uses the Expanded Sleep EDF public dataset.

articleTitle: The Comparative Study Between I and L Dipole Antenna Topologies for Space Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to compare the performances in terms of reflection coefficient (S11) and adaptation of the dipole antenna in I and L topology at the S band frequency for CubeSat applications. This antenna can transmit at a frequency of 3 GHz and fulfills a set of features according to the required specifications including image downloading. The proposed antenna has a simple, lightweight design, low manufacturing cost and is very compact, it is designed using an FR-4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.4 and a thickness of 1.6 (mm) and fed by a coaxial line which has an impedance of 50. The results showed that the proposed antenna of topology L gives better results compared to the one with topology I in terms of reflection coefficient and bandwidth, these are respectively (-25 dB, 32,3dB) and (1.67 GHz, 1GHz).

articleTitle: AI-Driven Triage: A Graph Neural Network Approach for Prehospital Emergency Triage Patients in IoMT-Based Telemedicine Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Improper triage, overcrowding in the emergency department (ED), and long wait times for patients are some of the problems that arise from emergency triage due to a lack of medical and human resources. In emergency departments, proper patient triage is crucial for determining the urgency and appropriateness of treatment by evaluating the severity of each patient's condition. In most cases, a human operator will use the knowledge and data gathered from patient management to perform triage tactics. Hence, it is a method with the possibility of causing problems in high-priority interconnections. Currently, typical triage systems primarily rely on human recommendations, which are susceptible to personal convictions and error. Methods that maximize data collection and remove mistakes in patient triage processing are being developed with an increasing amount of interest in utilizing artificial intelligence (AI). We develop and deploy an AI module to control the distribution of emergency triage patients in EDs. We use data from past emergency room visits to educate the medical decision-making process. Patients are properly sorted into triage groups because of data including vital signs, symptoms, and an ECG. Test results have shown that the proposed algorithm is better than the currently used state-of-the-art triage techniques. In our opinion, the methods used will help healthcare professionals forecast the severity index, which in turn will help them direct the proper patient management protocols and allocate resources.

articleTitle: Laser Scanning Modalities Revisited
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The aim of this study is to compare advantages and disadvantages of some of the most common laser scanning modalities: raster scanning (that is considered the gold standard in laser scanning systems), spiral, Lissajous, and, Rhodonea curves-based scanning (the latter generated for example by Risley prisms). Aspects such as linearity, field-of-view (FOV), and fill factor (FF) have been explored for these modalities. The first two have the potential of linearity and distortion-free, with the drawback of being slow. The latter two are inherently non-linear but with high scan speed. In this study, simulations were performed with MathCAD 15 for spiral, Rhodonea curve-based, and Lissajous scan patterns. Raster and Lissajous scan patterns were experimentally validated with in-house two-dimensional (2D) galvanometer scanners (GS). For spiral scan patterns, Fermat, Archimedean and constant linear velocity (CLV) scanning were examined, in terms of uniformity and distortion. The first one has distortions at margins, with the number of generated spires equal to the frequency; the latter two are uniform and presenting distortions in the center of the scanning pattern, due to increased beam density in that region. The Cornu spiral was also briefly approached. The main focus has been on Lissajous based scan patterns; its FF analysis was carried out for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{x}=32$</tex> Hz frequency on the horizontal axis and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{y}=1$</tex> to 32 Hz adjustable frequencies on the vertical axis. The cases of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{y}=30$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{y}=31$</tex> Hz were considered, to compare the even- and the odd-numbered case. For the latter, the FF was double. The frequency ratios <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{y}:f_{x}=3: 2; 7: 3$</tex> and 7: 10 were considered for validations, with a good match between simulations and experimental results.

articleTitle: High Voltage DC-DC Converter for Safety Beacons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a high voltage DC-DC converter tailored for powering circuits that operate at relative high voltages (HVs) but require low current consumption. These kinds of circuits, such as LED beacons, are commonly used in various industries including automotive, biomedical, and aerospace, where high-power and HV circuit testing is essential. The device under test (DUT), which can be another DC-DC converter, a charger or anything else, is supplied with a very HV, which could damage the beacon or expose the operator. Safety is a priority during testing. To address this, a robust DC-DC converter was developed to convert high input voltages, from various DUTs, into a stable output voltage suitable for low-current, lower-voltage applications, such as a LED beacon. The compact design of the converter makes it ideal for integration into testing environments without adding clutter and occupying space. It then plays a key role in ensuring safety in every test laboratory, contributing to a more secure testing process. The theoretical design is presented and then confirmed by simulation. In the end, the prototype of the proposed final product is tested, assuring correct operation.

articleTitle: Real-Time GPS Mapping and Tracking Tool for Enhanced Radio Network Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Global Positioning System (GPS) technology has transformed navigation and positioning management in a variety of fields, including transportation, logistics, and complex military and civilian applications. GPS provides an accurate and efficient way to determine location and time by using a network of artificial satellites that transmit radio signals to GPS devices on the ground. In the military, GPS technology is essential for precise navigation, coordination and system guidance, providing significant advantages. It enhances situational awareness and enables rapid response capabilities that are critical to mission success. In addition, the integration of GPS with other technologies, such as communications and surveillance systems, significantly increases the efficiency and safety of operations. The present work aims to develop a real-time monitoring application for radio stations, combining specific aspects of radio communications, Python programming and networking, so that the final result represents a complete and efficient alternative solution for managing and monitoring other resources in real time.
